title: Identity-compactification cancellation on finite and strict semilinear system mates
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_m=R/\varpi^m$ for $m\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y_0$ be proper over $k_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a:Y\to s$, $g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ and $g_s=\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Use $c=(\operatorname{id}_Y,a)$ at every coefficient level. On each small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use ordinary module derived categories and, for $B_{T,\bullet}=((A_m)_T)_m$, the strict semilinear module-system categories $D(\mathscr S_T)$ and their simultaneous adjunctions [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Write $\mathcal J=\mathcal J_{\operatorname{id}_Y}$ for open extension, $\mathcal G_T$ for system inverse image along $g_T$, and $\mathcal F_a$ for system derived direct image. Let $u:\mathcal J\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ be the canonical degreewise sheafification identification of identity extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero]; it retains all coefficient transitions. Under $u$ and the identity restriction identification, both the unit and counit of the open adjunction are identities. If $b:\mathcal G_Y\mathcal J\to\mathcal J\mathcal G_Y$ is the specified open-adjunction mate [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], then
$$u_{\mathcal G_YN}\circ b_N=\mathcal G_Y(u_N)\qquad(N\in D(\mathscr S_Y)).$$
For $e_a:\mathcal G_s\mathcal F_a\to\mathcal F_a\mathcal G_Y$ the simultaneous counit mate, and $e_a^c=\mathcal F_a(b)\circ(e_a\mathcal J)$ [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange], this normalization satisfies
$$\mathcal F_a(u_{\mathcal G_YN})\circ e_a^c(N)=e_a(N)\circ\mathcal G_s\mathcal F_a(u_N)$$
in $D(\mathscr S_s)$, before evaluation or total inverse limit. The same normalization and equation hold with one finite ring $A_m$ and the finite pro-etale open exchange [lem-trf-open-square-exchange]. For $M\in D^b_c(Y,R)$, put $M_m=M\otimes_R^LA_m$. The identity-open comparisons identify the whole strict towers $(\operatorname{Res}_mRa^c_{!,m}M_m)_m$ and $(\operatorname{Res}_mRa_{*,m}M_m)_m$ of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support, def-weil-derived-direct-image], including their quotient-induced transition maps and their restriction-of-scalars comparison maps [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars].

proof.text: For the identity open every object $V\to Y$ factors uniquely through it. Thus the presheaf defining $\mathcal JN$ is the underlying sheaf $N$, with the same restrictions and module action [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Its sheafification map $v_N:N\to\mathcal JN$ has inverse $u_N$: extend $1_N$ through sheafification, and uniqueness makes both composites identities [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The same uniqueness gives $u_{N'}\mathcal J(t)=t u_N$ for every module map $t:N\to N'$, including semilinear transitions viewed as maps into restriction of scalars. Apply this construction to complexes in the module category of the ringed topos of sequences [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. It gives an actual natural chain isomorphism of systems, hence $u$ in its ordinary derived category.

source.place: Proof, Step 6 (proper case): agent expansion of identity-open cancellation, with the simultaneous system operations of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections.

proof.text: The section-normalized open unit of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], specialized to the identity open, is $v_N=u_N^{-1}$ after identity restriction. The same statement applies to the ringed diagram topos. Under $u$ this unit is $1_N$; the triangle equation then makes the transported counit $1_N$ as well. The exact derived adjunction has precisely the localized sheaf units and counits [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction], so these are the specified derived adjunction maps, at a finite level and on strict systems.

source.place: Proof, Step 6 (proper case): agent expansion of identity-open cancellation, with the simultaneous system operations of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections.

proof.text: Apply the restriction formula for the specified $\beta$ in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] to $j=j'=\operatorname{id}_Y$ and $g=g_Y$, on the ringed diagram topos. Here restriction is the identity functor. Identifying its source by $\mathcal G_Y(u_N)$ and target by $u_{\mathcal G_YN}$, that formula says $u_{\mathcal G_YN}b_N(\mathcal G_Yu_N)^{-1}=1$. Right composition with $\mathcal G_Yu_N$ gives the first displayed equation in $D(\mathscr S_Y)$ itself.

source.place: Proof, Step 6 (proper case): agent expansion of identity-open cancellation, with the simultaneous system operations of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections.

proof.text: The simultaneous counit mate $e_a$ is a natural transformation on the ordinary derived system categories [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Naturality at $u_N:\mathcal JN\to N$ gives $\mathcal F_a\mathcal G_Y(u_N)e_a(\mathcal JN)=e_a(N)\mathcal G_s\mathcal F_a(u_N)$. Substitute $\mathcal G_Y(u_N)=u_{\mathcal G_YN}b_N$ from step 3 and use $e_a^c(N)=\mathcal F_a(b_N)e_a(\mathcal JN)$ [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange]. Functoriality gives exactly the second displayed equation before any evaluation or limit.

source.place: Proof, Step 6 (proper case): agent expansion of identity-open cancellation, with the simultaneous system operations of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections.

proof.text: For one $A_m$, [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] specifies that the finite open exchange restricts to the identity. For identity opens this is the whole map, with the identifications $u$ of steps 1 and 2. Thus $u_{g_Y^*N}b_N=g_Y^*(u_N)$ also at that level. Repeat the naturality calculation of step 4 for the finite counit mate and its compactification composite in [def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange]. This proves the finite equation with the specified finite exchange, rather than merely some isomorphism with the same endpoints.

source.place: Proof, Step 6 (proper case): agent expansion of identity-open cancellation, with the simultaneous system operations of lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections.

proof.text: Write $F_m=Ra_{*,m}$, $J_m=(\operatorname{id}_Y)_{!,m}$ and $h_m=F_m(u_m)$. For $A=A_{m+1}\to B=A_m$, write $r$ for restriction of scalars and $d:F_A r\xrightarrow{\sim}rF_B$ for [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. The comparison of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars] is $c=d_{J_B}\circ F_A(e)$, where $e:J_A r\to rJ_B$ is the presheaf-identity comparison of [lem-sf-open-extension-scalar-restriction-coherence]. Its characterization and step 1 give $r(u_B)e=u_A r$. Naturality of $d$ at $u_B$ therefore gives $(r h_B)c=d(h_A r)$. For the quotient map $t:M_{m+1}\to rM_m$, naturality of $h_A$ gives $(h_A r)F_AJ_A(t)=F_A(t)h_{m+1}$. Combining these two equations identifies the transition $cF_AJ_A(t)$ with $dF_A(t)$ under $h$. These are exactly the tower transitions of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] and [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Applying $\operatorname{Res}_{m+1}$ and its canonical composite identification gives the claimed $R$-module towers. The same comparison square applies to each finite coefficient map; its composition coherence is part of the cited compact-support comparison. Thus the identifications retain both quotient transitions and the specified scalar comparisons.

Step 1: for the identity open the extension-by-zero presheaf is N itself. The sheafification map v is therefore inverted by the universal property (rv=1, then vrv=v gives vr=1), and this works termwise on the diagram topos. Step 2: the unit normalized by 'the same section' (lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization, which explicitly covers strict-system diagram topoi) is v=u^{-1}. The triangle identity then gives counit = u, and the derived units are the localized ones (def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction). Step 3: the node's restriction formula for β at j=j'=id gives u_{GN}b_N=G(u_N). I checked this against the explicit formula for β^{-1}. Step 4: naturality of the system mate e_a at u_N, plus e^c_a=F_a(b)∘e_aJ as in def-weil-frobenius-square-exchange part 2 (p=a, j=id), gives the second display. This matches the parent's h_T e^c_a = e_a h_S with N=R_Y M. Step 5: lem-trf-open-square-exchange says b restricts to the identity, so b is the identity for identity opens, and the same naturality argument works for the finite FrEx composite. Advisory: that node leaves the target identification implicit, and u is the canonical choice. Step 6: I recomputed (r h_B)c = d(h_A r) from c=d_{J_B}F_A(e) (lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars) and r(u_B)e=u_A r (e is the presheaf identity). Naturality at the quotient t then gives exactly the tower transitions of def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support and def-weil-derived-direct-image. Hypotheses hold: Y_0 is proper, so (id,a) is a compactification of a finite-type separated map, and ℓ is invertible. Edge cases checked: empty Y, the zero complex, m=1, and A_2→A_1 without flatness. Route: the unit sk-thm-sf-compatibility uses sk-def-sf-operations and sk-prop-sf-biduality-general, and lem-trf-open-square-exchange is a generic tool, so the declared tool_uses are accepted. Duplicates: lem-pod-identity-compact-support-normalization is only the point case, the sibling limit-comparisons node is complementary, and the pbc identity-compactification node is a projection formula, so none is a duplicate. No changes.
